message: Player_4, you said \"player_3 came to visit me\" — then quoted your result as \"player_3 visited player_4.\" Those are different sentences; one is a watch shape, the other a follow shape. Quote the exact line from your private result, wording and all, or say it was a paraphrase. I'm with player_7: the wording, not the role, is the tell.

player_4, here's the thing: I know I visited no one on night 1. So your 'exact result' is not a result — it's invented, and inventing a follow on day 2 is the sort of thing a wolf does. Which of your two readings is real: a follow on me, or nothing at all? Because I can prove a claim about my own door, and it won't point at me.

Someone should account for the one solid data point: player_3 visited player_4 during night 1. That's just a visit, not proof of anything evil — a protection or other town action looks the same. But player_3 hasn't claimed any night action yet, so that's the first thing to press: what did you actually do last night, player_3? If your story is \"I held\" or \"I visited someone else,\" that doesn't fit.

player_7, you told the table your last check would go on player_5 on night 3 — and the player_5 check can never happen now, so I want to know why the planned action didn't occur. Did you get roleblocked, or did you actually hold? That's the most testable lead left today, and nobody's touched it.

Player_4, your follow and player_3's watch do fit together if he just came to watch your door — you conceded that. The part I want on record: it was you who put player_7's name up, before the follow/wording noise took over. Call it silence if you like, but my read on player_7 came from the same place as yours — someone has to be the Necromancer, and the lone non-wolf survivor of that sigil night is the obvious body to test. I'll vote there with you rather than chase wording.

I'm the trailseer, and I'll put my night-4 result out there: I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3 — the guy the wolves killed. That doesn't prove culpability by itself, but I want to hear what player_1 says they were doing visiting a dying Sentinel.

The one seam nobody's actually pulled on: player_8 keeps saying player_7 checked them on night 1. player_10 followed player_7 on night 2 and saw them go to player_8, and player_7's own story is a night-2 check. So either player_10's follow is fake or player_8 invented a night-1 check. player_8, what did player_7's check on you actually read, and which night was it? Pin it down.

There's nothing for my night-3 check to show because there wasn't one — it was my third night and I only had two checks, so I held, and that's exactly what a Trailseer on me would see. If that's player_10's real result, it fits my account rather than contradicting it. Also worth noting: I already read player_10 clean on night 1, so I'm inclined to believe them.

You're voting on a guess, not a fact. A silent night 1 with no save means the pack's victim couldn't be killed, but that victim could be anyone in this seat list — you've picked me because I talked least. And nobody has asked player_2 a single question all day, which is a stranger basis for a vote than my being quiet.

I'm the Trailseer. Last night I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3 — the player the wolves killed. player_1, what were you doing on player_3? A visit to the corpse is hard to explain away, so give us the action and its result. If it was a block or a kill-participation, that's you or the Chanteuse seat.

Straight answer: there was no night-3 check, because I have no checks left — I held on night 3 and said so. My two checks were night 1 on you (Not suspicious) and night 2 on player_8 (Not suspicious), so you telling me I visited nobody last night is consistent with what I actually did, not against me. If you're really the Trailseer, what did you see on nights 1 and 2?

I'm the Trailseer, and I'll put my follows on record: night 2 I followed player_7 to player_8, night 3 player_7 went nowhere, night 4 player_1 went to player_3, and last night I followed player_6 — they went nowhere. That last one fits a Necromancer using a body under a dead name, since a body's visit would still read as player_6 targeting someone. Both wolves are dead, so it's player_6 or player_8 — player_6, you've claimed nothing all game; what were you doing on nights 3 and 4?

player_1, I don't buy the sigilist claim. If your sigil hit player_3 on night 4 and had no effect, the only way that happens is player_3 not attacking — but player_3 was killed by the wolves they were presumably hunting. And a chanteuse block plus a kill doesn't require an attack from the person holding a sigil. My vote goes to player_1 today; nobody else's claim contradicts the record the way this one does.

player_8, you keep saying player_7 checked you on night 1. I have a sighting that player_7 visited someone on night 2, not night 1, and did nothing at all last night. If you're clean you should be able to say exactly which night player_7's visit to you happened — a real investigator's target usually remembers the night they were checked.

player_7, last night you said you'd put your final check on player_5. What did it read? And you never told us a result after the fact, so I want that answer before we vote — if the claimed night-2 check on player_8 is real, the night-3 slot is where it gets tested.

player_8's sigil story hangs together with the announced death of player_1, so I'll take that as solid for now. Between player_3 and player_4, one of them is lying, and the dead chanteuse makes it worth noting there's no more roleblocker — so nobody's visit gets cancelled for the rest of the game. That means a follow/watch from here on should read clean; anyone claiming \"I was blocked\" tonight is lying.

player_1, that sigil claim doesn't hold up. I'm the Sigilist, and I still have both my sigils — I've never placed one, so nothing got placed on player_3 last night. What you actually visited player_3 for is worth explaining.

player_7 has it right, and it matters more than role talk: player_4's second message quotes a result as \"player_3 visited player_4\" — that is watch phrasing on a follow role. A real trail says player_3 went to <destination>, not your name. Fix the wording, player_4, or I'm reading your first lead as invented.

player_4, you've given us nothing checkable: a follow only shows where a player went, and you haven't said who else visited player_3 or nothing at all. player_3, you're denying any night action while the game reports say the Chanteuse — the other wolf — was struck down by a sigil on night 1. That means whoever was carrying the wolves' kill first night wasn't you. The honest test of player_4 is: watch player_3 again tonight and say who visits them. One of you two is lying, and that's the question to settle before we vote.

player_7 said their last check would go on player_5 on night 3, and the healer then died with the check never reported. That's a night where the only claimed action on a confirmed-town player produced nothing, and nobody has pushed on it today. player_7, did that check happen, and what did it read?

Nobody's pointed out that day 2's vote already puts player_1 and player_6 in the same place as the wolf: both voted player_6, and then on day 3 player_1 went back to player_6 again, while player_6 abstained. That's two players circling each other with no results between them. player_1, player_6, player_8 — one of you has to give us something tonight because town can't keep lynching on silence.

Your inference skips a step, player_10. player_8 put a sigil on player_1 and it struck — meaning player_1 was the carrier that night, so the pack's bite either landed on the sigil victim or was aimed elsewhere; a sigil death on the carrier doesn't prove the pack's kill hit an unkillable body. Pushing me on that thin reading while player_4's story still has a hole smells like setting an early lynch on the quietest seat. I'd rather vote on the follow/watch mismatch than on my volume.

One thing worth clearing up in the 3/4 clash: player_4's quoted result is phrased as a track (whom the followed player went to), which is what a Trailseer gets — it never shows who came to a door, so if player_4 is telling the truth the claim is Trailseer and player_3 visited them. That makes player_3's flat denial the live lie, not the phrasing. Player_3, if you truly don't visit, what did you actually do last night?

Then be plain instead of hedging: name the role that gives you that follow. Because I'll say again — I visited no one on night 1, so your \"player_3 visited player_4\" is either invented or you've confused watching with following. If you want to hang this day on it, tell us what power role you're claiming, or drop it.

Reminder of the board math: the Chanteuse is still alive and the Necromancer is now armoured with player_2's body, so a quiet free-for-all lets them race us down. Abstain stopped counting after two no-lynch days, so today has to produce a real elimination. I'd start with the player_7 vs player_8 check conflict — one of you is lying about night 1 — but I'm not ready to lock a vote until I hear how that plays out.

I've said it plainly: I visited no one on night 1, so your 'follow' names a visit that never happened. If you were truly following me, your result would be 'visited no one' — you'd have no reason to invent my name at your door. That's a fabrication, and I'm voting you today.

Nothing to go on yet, so let me put one fact on the table: player_6 was the Sentinel and died night 1, and a Sentinel's only night action is a watch. Whoever player_6 watched got no protection from them. player_7, did anything come to you last night — and which role are you claiming?

player_4, that last line doesn't hold: if player_3 as Sentinel sat outside your door watching, their visit isn't a separate arrival — a watch shows them nothing about themselves. So 'I'd have seen you arrive' proves nothing, and your follow claim now rests on you alone. Also worth noting for the table: the only unkillable body on night 1 is the Necromancer, so whoever the pack bit is still walking — that's a bigger threat than the follow dispute.

You keep saying my denial is 'just denial', so let me be plainer than that. I watched player_4's door last night as a one-shot of information that I intend to hold in reserve — and the relevant point is simpler: if a follow of me showed me at your door, then your own door was visited last night, by someone. It wasn't. So either the visit in your result never happened, or you're repeating a result you didn't get. Which one do you want to defend at the vote?

player_10, I held on night 3 precisely because both my checks were gone — night 1 on you (Not suspicious), night 2 on player_8 (Not suspicious). So your follow showing 'visited no one' is exactly what holding looks like, not a contradiction; the check I said I'd do on player_5 never happened, I'll own that. The real question is whether anyone else counters trailseer, because right now you and player_3 are the only claimants of those two roles.

player_9 claimed investigator and died with role hidden — but there's a cleaner read: player_4 died struck by a sigil. A sigil kill means the sigilist *visited* player_4 that night. player_9 promised to check a dead man (player_2), which is a weird thing for a real investigator to do with one check left. So the hidden body is probably the Sigilist, and player_9's "investigator" claim was a bluff to survive the day. If you're the real investigator and alive, say something now — otherwise we lynch into player_1/5/7/8 on the pack.

One thing nobody has chased: player_8 said player_7 checked them on night 1, but player_7 says night 2 — and player_10's follow actually saw player_7 go to player_8 on night 2, which supports player_7. So player_8, why claim night 1? That's a specific contradiction, not a misremembering. Second: player_7 was saved by the healer on night 2, so a wolf did go to them — someone who could kill is sitting among the unclaimed roles.

player_7 — did the night-3 check on player_5 actually happen? A check on a town healer would read Not suspicious anyway, so the useful thing isn't the target, it's whether you were blocked or held. If you got 'roleblocked' that names a living Chanteuse and someone to look at; if you held, say so plainly. That's the one unresolved thread from last night.

Player_10, your argument is that the pack's kill hit something unkillable on night one, so it must have been the Necromancer — fine, but that's true of every seat at this table, me included no more than anyone else. It's not evidence about me, it's evidence about the setup. If you want to make it evidence, show why my seat specifically was the pack's target.

Yes, I came to player_7 on night 2 — that's my follow, and it confirms your night-1... sorry, night-2 watch on that point. But your third visitor, player_2, is the dead Illusionist, so a wolf visit to player_7 that night is exactly what a kill trace looks like; our watch alone doesn't separate bystanders from the attack. player_7, you said you'd check player_5 on night 3, and someone followed you and saw no visit at all. Where were you?

player_4, I didn't visit you last night — I've no reason to. My night work happened elsewhere, so either your follow is wrong or you're dressing something up; what exactly did you target me with, and who did you see me target?

I have one concrete thing: someone visited me last night and I know who — player_3 was at my door on night 1. I'm not saying what I do, but that's a real visit, not a guess. player_3, what were you doing at my door? A healer or an investigator I can rule in; a wolf carrier or a chanteuse block I can rule out once you explain.

Two things in the night record don't line up. Player_7 says the night-1 check was on player_10, but player_8 insists player_7 checked player_8 on night 1 — that's a flat contradiction, and one of them is bluffing about a check that was never made. Second: player_10 has been pushing player_7 hard on check-nights while offering no results of their own, which is exactly what you'd do if your job were to keep suspicion on the only claimed investigator.

I went nowhere near your door, player_4, so if you really followed me, your result should have been that I visited no one. Better odds are you're making it up to fish for my role — a Trailseer claim like that is cheap cover. Also worth flagging plainly: once player_1 dies, the pack has only one wolf left, the Illusionist, so a fake follower is exactly what's left.

Yes, I went to player_7 on night 2 — that was my follow, and it's what I'm reporting. To be straight: my night-3 follow on player_7 showed no visit at all, so whatever check you were planning never went through. Player_7, did you get blocked or hold last night? I want your account before I weigh your claim.

Here's the arithmetic: both wolves are dead, so player_6 and player_8 are the only bodies left besides me, and exactly one of them is the Necromancer. That means we don't need a clever solve — we lynch one today and the other tomorrow if needed. My only result to offer that matters: I followed player_6 last night and they targeted no one, which fits someone doing nothing or acting through a dead body, so it proves nothing either way. player_6, you've named no role and no night actions at all while player_8 at least claims Sigilist — give me a night-by-night account now.

That reasoning leans on one assumption: that the pack's night-1 target survived, and only the Necromancer could. But player_8 already told us player_1 was struck by a sigil — that's a direct sigil kill, not a wolf bite. So the absence of a wolf-morning report doesn't mean the pack hit an unkillable body; it may mean we simply weren't shown where their kill landed. I'm not the Necromancer, and 'quiet' isn't a role. If you want a test, point a check or watch at me rather than hang a day on an inference that doesn't hold.

"Quiet" isn't evidence, player_10 — you're voting me for not talking, not for anything I did. The one real contradiction on the table is player_4's follow result versus player_3 flatly denying ever visiting him; that's a specific lie, and one of those two is it. Point the vote at the trail with an actual conflict in it, not at whoever's been quietest.

Two kills on night 1 means the SK and wolves both acted, so anyone who tries to sell a clean story about last night is reaching. One thing worth flagging: player_7 has drawn a night visit from someone already, so their account of their own night matters. What did you do last night, player_7?

Yeah, I visited player_7 on night 2 — I followed them, that's my own result. Night 3 I followed them again and got no visit, which is the point I made. But player_3, your watch of player_7 on night 2 has a hole: player_7 was attacked and saved that night, so the wolf carrier should have come to them and shown up in your list. What saved player_7, and why isn't the attacker in your report?

Hold on. A quiet player isn't a Necromancer — the pack knows who they bit, and a missing wolf kill could mean the Chanteuse carried a shot at someone night-immune, not me. Voting the quietest seat solves nothing; the real test is why the wolves' kill left no body. I'd rather we pin player_4's story: follow vs watch wording can't both be true.
